channel.title: Honda recalls — Car Recall Tracker
channel.description: NHTSA vehicle safety recalls explained in plain English.

item.title: Honda CMX500 and CMX300 motorcycles: handlebar screw can detach
item.description: A small screw that locks the handlebars in position on these Honda motorcycles can loosen and fall out. If it drops down between the frame and the steering stem, it can get in the way of your steering and cause a crash or injury. Honda does not have the final fix ready yet. Warning letters are expected to be mailed around September 21, 2026, and a second letter will follow once parts are available, expected in winter 2026. Dealers will then install a new screw with thread lock.

item.title: Honda Odyssey backup camera can fail from water
item.description: Water can get inside the backup camera on these minivans. When that happens, the picture may not come up on the dashboard screen after you shift into reverse. You lose the view directly behind the van, so it is easier to back into something, or someone, that the mirrors do not show. Federal rules require that picture to appear, which is why this is a recall. The dealer replaces the camera at no charge to you.

item.title: Honda, Acura SUVs: rear frame can rust through
item.description: These vehicles were sold in states that salt the roads in winter. The rear subframe, the metal frame that holds the rear suspension to the body, can rust badly where the suspension bolts onto it. If it rusts through, a rear suspension part such as a control arm can come loose. The back of the vehicle can then wander or slide and you could lose control. Honda's full repair is not ready yet and is expected in fall 2026.

item.title: Honda CR-V and Accord Hybrid tire kit cap flies off
item.description: These hybrids come with a tire repair kit instead of a spare tire. Inside the kit is a bottle of sealant you squeeze into a flat tire. Pressure can build up inside that bottle while you use it, and the cap can pop off. A cap flying off under pressure can hit you or anyone standing nearby and cause an injury. Honda has already mailed a warning letter, and the parts needed for the final repair are expected in fall 2026.

item.title: Honda and Acura seat sensor may cause unintended airbag deployment
item.description: A sensor under the front passenger seat measures the weight of whoever is sitting there so the car knows how to use the airbags. That sensor can crack and short out. If it does, the airbags can go off in an unintended way during a crash, which can hurt the people inside. This recall covers a long list of Honda and Acura models and expands an earlier recall. Dealers will put in new seat weight sensors.

item.title: Honda Odyssey side airbags may deploy without a crash
item.description: A programming mistake in the computer that controls the airbags can make the side airbags and the curtain airbags along the windows go off when they should not, with no crash happening. An airbag that fires unexpectedly can injure whoever is sitting next to it. Dealers will reload the software in the airbag control computer, or replace that computer if reloading is not enough, free of charge. Honda mailed letters to affected owners on May 27, 2026.

item.title: Honda CB1000SP motorcycle fuel hose may come loose
item.description: On these motorcycles, the hose that carries gasoline from the fuel tank to the engine can come disconnected at the tank. If that happens, gas leaks out while you ride. The fuel can spill near the rear tire, which can make you lose control, and gasoline near anything hot or sparking can catch fire. A dealer will replace the fuel hose and secure a nearby wiring harness so the hose stays put.

item.title: Honda Rebel motorcycle handlebar screw can fall out
item.description: On these Honda CMX300, CMX500 and CL500 motorcycles, a small screw that locks the handlebar in place can work loose and drop out. If the loose screw falls into the gap between the frame and the steering stem, it can jam your steering and stop you from turning the way you want, which could cause a crash or injury. Dealers replace the screw and add a thread-locking compound so the new one stays tight. The work is free.

item.title: Honda and Acura models: driver's seat may be loose
item.description: The fasteners holding the driver's seat cushion frame may not have been tightened enough at the factory, so the driver's seat can be loose. A seat that is not solidly attached may not hold the driver in place in a crash, which means a higher chance of injury. The vehicles also do not meet the federal safety rule for seating systems. Dealers will replace the driver's seat cushion frame at no charge.

item.title: Honda CBR650R wiring damage kills lights and horn
item.description: On some 2024-2025 Honda CBR650R motorcycles, engine vibration can rub and damage the wiring for the turn signal switch. Damaged wiring can short out and blow a fuse. When that fuse goes, you lose your turn signals, your brake light, your speedometer and your horn all at once. Other drivers can no longer see when you are turning or slowing down. The dealer inspects that wiring and repairs it if needed.

item.title: Honda CB1000SP motorcycle engine may seize or leak oil
item.description: Some 2025 Honda CB1000SP motorcycles were built with pistons and piston rings that were not made correctly. Over time this can wear out an internal engine bearing. If that bearing fails, the engine can lock up and stop the rear wheel from turning, or engine oil can leak out onto the rear tire. Oil can also drip onto the hot exhaust. Honda has told owners about the danger, but the actual fix is not ready yet.

item.title: Honda CBR600RR engine flaw can lock rear wheel
item.description: The cylinder head, a major part at the top of the engine, may have been made incorrectly on these motorcycles. That flaw can cause a rod bearing inside the engine to fail. If it does, the rear wheel can suddenly lock up, or engine oil can leak out onto the rear tire. Oil that reaches hot exhaust parts can also start a fire. Honda will replace the entire engine, but the replacement parts are not ready yet.

item.title: Wheelchair van restraints may not lock in Odyssey, Pacifica, Sienna
item.description: These minivans were converted by Vantage Mobility so a wheelchair can ride inside. The wheelchair is held down by belt-style restraints with retractors that are supposed to lock, much like a seat belt locks. On these vans, the retractors may fail to lock, so the wheelchair is not really tied down. If it is not secured, the chair and the person in it can roll or tip while the van is moving, braking, or turning.

item.title: Honda Accord Hybrid can lose drive power while driving
item.description: A software mistake in one of the computers that manages your hybrid system can make it reset itself while you are driving. When that happens, the car can suddenly stop sending power to the wheels, so you lose the ability to accelerate. This can happen with no warning while the vehicle is moving. Honda has a corrected version of the software, and a dealer will load it into your car at no cost to you.

item.title: Honda CB1000SP Hornet shift lever bolt may fall out
item.description: On these Honda CB1000SP Hornet SP motorcycles, the bolt that the gearshift pedal pivots on can work its way loose and fall out. If that happens while you are riding, you cannot change gears at all — you would be stuck in whichever gear you were already in, with no way to shift up or down. Being unable to shift in traffic or on the highway can easily lead to a crash. A dealer will replace the pivot bolt.

item.title: Honda Africa Twin horn and high beam may fail
item.description: The wiring inside the left handlebar switch on these motorcycles can corrode — the metal rusts and stops carrying electricity properly. When that happens, the horn may quit working, or you may not be able to flip the headlight from low beam to high beam. Honda says the motorcycle no longer meets the federal rule covering lights and related equipment. A dealer will replace the entire left handlebar switch unit at no cost.

item.title: Acura and Honda brake pedal can shift out of position
item.description: The brake pedal in these Acura and Honda models is held in place by a small pin, and that pin was not fastened correctly at the factory. Over time the pedal can slip out of its normal position. If that happens, pressing the pedal may not slow or stop the vehicle the way you expect. Honda also says the affected vehicles do not meet federal rules for brake systems and for lamps and reflectors.

item.title: Honda CR-V Hybrid fuel hose can leak gasoline
item.description: On certain 2025 Honda CR-V Hybrids, the hose that carries gasoline from the tank toward the engine may not have been installed correctly at the factory, which lets fuel leak out. Leaking gasoline only needs a spark or a hot surface to catch fire. You might notice a strong gas smell, or wet spots and drips under the vehicle. Dealers will install a new fuel hose along with a cover for the connector so it seals properly.

item.title: Honda motorcycles may leak engine oil onto rear tire
item.description: A sealing bolt on the engine case may have been made incorrectly. If it does not seal properly, engine oil can seep out and drip onto the rear tire. Oil on a tire makes it slippery and can cause you to lose control of the motorcycle, especially while braking, cornering, or riding on wet pavement. Dealers will replace the crankcase sealing bolt at no charge, and owner letters went out in July 2025.

item.title: Honda CB300R headlight can flicker or quit
item.description: On these motorcycles the headlight can flicker or shut off completely while you are riding. If it goes dark at night or in bad weather, you lose the light you need to see the road ahead, and drivers around you lose an important clue that a motorcycle is there at all. Honda traced the problem to the headlight assembly itself, and dealers will install a new one at no cost. Owner letters went out in May 2025.

item.title: Honda ADV160 Scooter Can Lose Power From Broken Gear
item.description: A small gear that drives the engine's oil pump can fail. When it does, the scooter can suddenly stop pulling while you are riding. Losing power in traffic, on a hill, or in the middle of an intersection can easily lead to a crash or an injury. Honda dealers will install a new oil pump driven gear at no cost. Letters went out to owners on August 6, 2025.

item.title: Honda CB650R and CBR650R gear shift arm can fall off
item.description: On some 2024 Honda CB650R and CBR650R motorcycles, the bolts holding the gear shift arm — the lever you press with your foot to change gears — can work loose and come off. If that happens, you cannot change gears at all while you are riding. Honda dealers will put on a new gear shift arm at no cost to you. Honda began mailing letters to owners in 2025.

item.title: Honda Pilot third-row seat belt trapped behind side panel
item.description: On some 2025 Honda Pilots, the passenger-side seat belt in the third row was routed the wrong way at the factory, so the belt gets caught behind the plastic side panel next to the seat. When that happens, the belt will not pull out and latch the way it should, and whoever sits there cannot buckle up properly. In a crash, that passenger would not be held in place. Dealers will inspect the belt and route it correctly.

item.title: Acura and Honda Pilot software glitch can stall engine
item.description: The computer that controls how fuel is fed to the engine has a software bug on these Acura and Honda models. Because of it, the engine can stall or suddenly lose power while you are driving. Losing power in traffic or on the highway raises the risk of a crash. The dealer will reload corrected software into that computer at no charge; owner letters were mailed in March 2025.

item.title: Honda Pilot and Passport fuel pipe may leak gas
item.description: The pipe you put gas into connects to a neck tube on the fuel tank. On these Passports and Pilots, those two pieces can come apart, and gasoline can leak out. Leaking fuel near anything hot or sparking can start a fire. Dealers will inspect the parts and repair them if needed, free of charge. Letters went to owners in January 2025, so many of these vehicles may already be fixed. If you smell gas, get it checked right away.

item.title: Honda CRF1100 Africa Twin can stall with Wheelie Control
item.description: These Africa Twin motorcycles have a software mistake in the computer that controls the fuel injection. When the Wheelie Control feature is switched on, that error can make the engine stall or suddenly lose power. Losing power without warning on a motorcycle can make it hard to stay in control or keep up with traffic. The repair is a software update for the fuel injection computer, which your Honda dealer loads free of charge.

item.title: Honda and Acura Driver's Seat May Be Loose
item.description: On certain Honda Accord, Accord Hybrid, Civic Sedan, Civic Hatchback, Pilot and HR-V vehicles and Acura Integra models, the driver's seat cushion frame may not have been tightened properly when the car was built. That can leave the driver's seat not firmly secured to the floor. These vehicles do not meet the federal safety standard for seating systems. Dealers will replace the driver's seat cushion frame at no cost to the owner.

item.title: Honda Gold Wing: engine bolt may break, locking rear wheel
item.description: Inside the engine of these Gold Wing motorcycles, the bolt that holds the main drive gear onto the crankshaft can snap. If it breaks, the engine can stall and the rear wheel can lock up. On a motorcycle, a rear wheel that suddenly stops turning can put you on the ground, and it can happen while you are riding. Honda mailed owner letters on December 30, 2024. A dealer will install a new primary drive gear bolt for free.

item.title: Honda Accord, CR-V and Civic fuel pump can leak
item.description: The high-pressure fuel pump on these cars can crack and let gasoline leak out. Leaking fuel near anything hot or sparking can start a fire. A dealer will inspect the pump and replace it if it needs it, at no cost to you. Honda mailed owner letters on February 20, 2025, so if you have not had this checked, book it now. If you ever smell gasoline or see fuel dripping under the car, call your dealer right away.

item.title: Honda CR-V Hybrid battery can spark and cause fire
item.description: Some 2023 CR-V Hybrids have parts inside the big battery pack that were not made correctly. A connection inside the pack can break and spark. That spark can cause a fire or injure someone. The same problem can also cut the power to the wheels while you are driving, meaning the vehicle could suddenly slow or stop in traffic. Honda dealers will replace the affected battery module at no cost to you.

item.title: Honda and Acura steering gearbox may make steering difficult
item.description: The steering gearbox — the part that turns your steering wheel motion into the wheels turning — may have been built wrong on these Honda and Acura models. Parts inside can rub too hard against each other, which can make the vehicle difficult to steer. Difficulty steering raises the chance of a crash. The dealer will replace a spring inside the gear and add or move grease around as needed, all free of charge.

item.title: Honda CR-V tires missing required date code marking
item.description: The code stamped on the tire sidewall that identifies each tire is missing its four-digit date section. That date is how tire makers and owners tell which tires are covered by a safety recall. Without it, you might never learn your tires were recalled and could keep driving on them. This recall is about that missing marking, which federal tire rules require, and Honda will replace the tires if needed.

item.title: Honda Fit and HR-V backup camera image may fail
item.description: Because of a design problem in the audio display's power circuit, the backup camera image may not come up at all when you start the car with a key. With no picture on the screen, it is easier to miss a person, pet, or object behind you while reversing. A dealer will reprogram the display audio unit for free. Important: if your vehicle was already repaired under the earlier recall 23V-046, it still needs this new repair.

item.title: Honda Ridgeline backup camera wiring can break
item.description: The wiring that runs to the backup camera in the tailgate can bend and flex until it breaks. When the wire breaks, the camera picture stops showing up on your dashboard screen, so you cannot see what is behind you when reversing. That blind spot makes it easier to back into something, or someone. Your Honda dealer will replace the tailgate wiring harness for the backup camera at no cost. Owner letters were mailed November 8, 2024.

item.title: Honda Passport and Ridgeline may lose steering control
item.description: A ball joint inside the steering gearbox can work loose and come apart from the steering rack. The steering rack is the part that turns your front wheels when you turn the wheel. If that joint separates, you can lose the ability to steer the vehicle. Honda dealers will inspect the steering gearbox and replace it if needed, at no charge. Owner letters went out in April 2024, so the inspection can be done now.

item.title: Honda Goldwing, CBR fuel pumps can fail and stall
item.description: The fuel pump inside the gas tank has a spinning part that may have been molded wrong. Over time it can warp and jam, so the pump stops sending gas to the engine. If that happens while you're riding, the engine can quit without warning, which is dangerous on a motorcycle in traffic. A Honda dealer will check the fuel pump and put in a new one if needed, at no cost to you.

item.title: Honda Odyssey and Acura RDX steering can rust, bind
item.description: The steering gearbox on these vehicles may not have been tightened properly when it was put together. A gearbox that is not tight lets water get inside, and the water causes rust. Rusted gears can start to bind, which means the steering may feel stiff or may not respond the way it should while you are driving. Honda dealers will replace the entire electric power steering rack on affected vehicles, free of charge to the owner.

item.title: Honda and Acura passenger seat sensor may crack, airbag risk
item.description: There is a sensor in the front passenger seat that senses the weight of whoever is sitting there. It tells the vehicle whether to turn the passenger airbag off — for example when the seat is empty or a small person is in it. On these vehicles the sensor can crack and short out, so the airbag may not switch off when it should. It could then go off in a crash when it was supposed to stay shut. Dealers replace the sensor free.

item.title: Honda and Acura fuel pump can fail, stalling engine
item.description: The fuel pump sits inside the gas tank and sends fuel to the engine. On these vehicles that pump can fail. When it does, the engine can stall while you are driving — losing power in traffic or on the highway raises the chance of a crash. A dealer will replace the entire fuel pump unit for free. This recall is an expansion of two earlier Honda fuel pump recalls covering additional vehicles.

item.title: Honda CR-V Hybrid battery cable can overheat in a crash
item.description: The cable running from the 12-volt battery along the outside of the frame is missing a fuse. A fuse is the small part that cuts the power if something goes wrong. Without it, a crash that damages the cable can let it short out or get very hot, and that can start a fire. The notice describes this happening in a crash, not during ordinary driving. A dealer will replace the cable with a corrected one.
